IGI Airport.

(c) Name of the accused persons : (1) Maninder Singh @ Rinku, S/o Sh. Shakti Singh (Declared PO).

(g) Date of institution of case : 15.04.2011 (h) Date of final arguments : 15.01.2024 (i) Date of Judgment : 16.01.2024 ABHISHEK KU  KUMAR Da  20  16 FIR No. 437/2004 State v. Maninder Singh & Anr Page No:- 1 BRIEF REASONS FOR THE DECISION OF THE CASE 1.
The briefs facts of the case are that on 29.09.2004, one pax with the name Mohan Raj Praveen arrived as a deportee from Dubai by flight no. EK-510, with passport bearing no. E-8582162.

1 preliminary inquiry, the pax told the clearing officer that he is the only son of his parents and studied upto class 10 th from DPS, Karol Bagh and his father was working in French Embassy.

sentences.text: Thereafter, it was found by the clearing officer that there was no branch of DPS in Karol Bagh and telephonic call to French embassy confirmed the fact that one Mohan Raj was working there but had 3 sons.

Thus, seeking prior permission, clearing officer went to French Embassy and met Mohan Raj, who told that he got the visa of UK on 23.07.2004 and his family went missing, for which he got a report lodged at PS Chankyapuri.

2. The clearing officer sternly interrogated the pax further, who disclosed that his original name was Mahender Singh s/o Shakti (PO) and obtained the passport from one Dwivedi at Bangla Sahib and went to Dubai for France with one Kuldeep Singh, who were together deported back from Dubai.
The status of departure and arrival of both the persons were confirmed from concerned airlines.
Accordingly, pax was handed over to PS alongwith travel documents and complaint.
Thus, FIR was registered under section 419/420/468/471/120B IPC and 12 of the Passport Act.

3. During the course of the investigation, the said pax disclosed that the agent Kuldeep Singh met him and his father, FIR No. 437/2004 State v. Maninder Singh & Anr ABHISHEK KUMAR Page No:- 2 KUMAR Date:
2024.01.16 16:46:08 +0530 who was recommended by some relatives already settled abroad and he asked for Rs 6 lacs to facilitate the journey and took Rs 1 lac as advance from his father and remaining amount was to be paid after reaching the destination.
He also disclosed that agent Kuldeep told him to reiterate the story of Dwivedi to the officials.

After further investigation and recording of the statement of the witnesses, the accused Kulddep Singh was arrested and the charge- sheet was filed under section 419/420/468/471/120B IPC and 12 of the Passport Act.
PROCEEDINGS BEFORE THE COURT 4.
After filing of the charge-sheet, the cognizance of the offence was taken and accused persons were summoned.
However, accused Kuldeep Singh put his appearance in the court and the accused Maninder Singh remained absent despite service.
Thereafter, following the procedure, he was declared PO.

Upon the appearance of the accused Kuldeep Singh, charge-sheet along with the relevant documents were supplied to the accused in compliance of Section 207 Cr.PC.
5.

Further, arguments on charge were heard and a charge was framed against the accused Kuldeep Singh under Section 120B IPC, 419 read with 120B IPC & section 12 of the Passport Act, to which the accused did not plead guilty and claimed trial.
Then, the matter proceeded for the prosecution evidence.
The prosecution evidence commenced on 27.01.2016 and was concluded on 15.12.2023.

The prosecution had cited 18 witnesses out of which it examined 7 witnesses as remaining witnesses were dropped as ABHISHEK KUMAR FIR No. 437/2004 State v. Maninder Singh & Anr KUMAR Date:
 2024.01.16 Page   16:46:23 +0530 State vs Maninder Singh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154998318/
2
they were not traceable and on account of admission of documents by the accused under section 294 CrPC.
The statement of the accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C was recorded on 15.01.2024.
Despite opportunity, the accused did not lead any defence evidence.
Accordingly, final arguments were heard on behalf of the State as well as on behalf of the accused and the matter was reserved for orders.

Before proceeding further to give findings, it will be pertinent to discuss the relevant provisions of law involved in the present case and also analyze the facts in the light of evidence led by the prosecution.
6. For easy reference and understanding, the provisions of law involved in the present case have been broadly classified into three categories i.e Criminal Conspiracy, Cheating and Passport Act.

sentences.text: Let us discuss these categories one by one hereinafter.
CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY 7.
The criminal conspiracy is a punishable offence under Section 120 B IPC, which is defined under Section 120A IPC.

In case titled as Rajendra alias Rajesh alias Raju v. State of NCT of Delhi (2019)
10 SCC 623, the hon'ble Apex Court has observed that it is trite law that the existence of three elements must be shown--a criminal object, a plan or a scheme embodying means to accomplish that object, and an agreement or understanding between two or more people to cooperate for the accomplishment of such object's.

entities.text:
Rajendra alias Rajesh alias Raju v. State of NCT of Delhi (2019)
10 SCC 623
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Digitally signed ABHISHEK by ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2024.01.16 16:46:30 +0530 FIR No. 437/2004 State v. Maninder Singh & Anr Page No:- 4 8.

Further in the case of Yogesh v. State of Maharashtra [(2008) 10 SCC 394], the honble Supreme Court of India in reference to criminal conspiracy has observed as follows:
"...25.

entities.text: Yogesh v. State of Maharashtra [(2008) 10 SCC 394]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is manifest that the meeting of minds of two or more persons for doing an illegal act or an act by illegal means is sine qua non of the criminal conspiracy but it may not be possible to prove the agreement between them by direct proof.
Nevertheless, existence of the conspiracy and its objective can be inferred from the surrounding circumstances and the conduct of the accused.
But the incriminating circumstances must form a chain of events from which a conclusion about the guilt of the accused could be drawn.

It is well settled that an offence of conspiracy is a substantive offence and renders the mere agreement to commit an offence punishable, even if an offence does not take place pursuant to the illegal agreement..."

9. To summarize, criminal conspiracy is an independent offence, which is punishable separately and can be proved either by way of direct proof or circumstantial evidence, only if essential ingredients as mentioned under Section 120A IPC are fulfilled.
Also, upon the proof of the same, the accused can be held liable for the commission of other substantive offences.

sentences.text: The offence pertaining to cheating is covered under Chapter 17 of the IPC under the heading 'of offences against property' and is covered from Section 415 to 420 IPC.
Section 420 i.e 'cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property' is an aggravated form of cheating, which provides for enhanced punishment.

11. In the offence of cheating, a person deceives another person fraudulently or dishonestly to deliver any property or consent to the retention of any property or intentionally induces another ABHISHEK KUMAR FIR No. 437/2004 State v. Maninder Singh & Anr KUMAR

Date:
 2024.01.16 Page  16:46:40 +0530 person to do or omit to do anything which he would not have done if he was not so deceived and such act has caused or is likely to cause damage, or harm in body, mind, reputation or property.

12. In the case of Iridium India Tel oftenecom Ltd. v. Motorola Inc., (2011) 1 SCC 74, the Honble Supreme Court of India while refering to Section 415 IPC has observed as follows:
"...68.

entities.text: Iridium India Tel oftenecom Ltd. v. Motorola Inc., (2011) 1 SCC 74
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A bare perusal of the aforesaid section would show that it can be conveniently divided into two parts.
The first part makes it necessary that the deception by the accused of the person deceived, must be fraudulent or dishonest.

Such deception must induce the person deceived to either: (a) deliver property to any person; or (b)
consent that any person shall retain any property.
The second part also requires that the accused must by deception intentionally induce the person deceived either to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit, if he was not so deceived.
Furthermore, such act or omission must cause or must be likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind, reputation or property.
Thus, it is evident that deception is a necessary ingredient for the offences of cheating under both parts of this section..."
PASSPORT ACT 13. Section 3 of the Passport Act provides that no person shall depart from, or attempt to depart from, India unless he holds in this behalf a valid passport or travel document.

14. Section 12 of the Act provides for offences and penalties and Section 12(1) states as follows:
Whoever- (a) contravenes the provisions of section 3; or (b) knowingly furnishes any false information or suppresses any material information with a. view to obtaining a passport or travel document under this Act or without lawful authority alters or attempts to alter or causes to alter the entries made in a passport or travel document; or State vs Maninder Singh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154998318/
4 (c) fails to produce for inspection his passport or travel document (whether issued under this Act or not) when called upon to do so by the prescribed authority; or ABHISHEK KUMAR FIR No. 437/2004 State v. Maninder Singh & Anr KUMAR Date: Page No:- 6 2024.01.16 16:46:47 +0530 (d) knowingly uses a passport or travel document issued to another person; or (e) knowingly allows another person to use a passport or travel document issued to him, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to 7 [two years or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees] or with both.

15. After understanding the relevant provisions of law involving the present case, let us move to analyse the facts which stands proved or not proved by taking into account the evidence which has been brought on record by the prosecution.
ANALYSIS OF THE PROSECUTION EVIDENCE 16.
In order to prove the registration of the present FIR, the prosecution had examined PW3 SI Ishwar Singh.
The witness has deposed that on 30.09.2004, he was working as a Duty Officer and at about 05:45 pm, he received rukka from Ct. Shashipal which was sent by SI N.K. Jha.
Further, the custody of the pax Maninder Singh was also handed over to him alnogwith the travel documents of the passenger.

Thereafter, he made endorsement on the rukka which is Ex.PW-3/A and registered the FIR which is Ex.PW3/B (OSR) and seized documents vide seizure memo Ex.PW3/C.
17.
During the cross examination of the witness, no material inconsistency could be brought on record with respect to the registration of the FIR.

The testimony of the PW-3 gets substantiated through PW-2, who confirmed the fact that the passenger Maninder Singh was apprehended ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR Date:
2024.01.16 FIR No. 437/2004 State v. Maninder Singh & Anr 16:46:57 +0530 Page No:- 7 and was sent to the PS alongwith the complaint and travel documents.

Thus,
the prosecution has been able to establish the authenticity of the FIR and the seizure of the travel documents.

18. The fact that one pax namely Maninder Singh @ Rinku arrived from Dubai on 30.09.2004 as a deportee stands confirmed from the testimony of PW-2 who was a clearing officer at counter no. 2 on the date of the arrival of the passenger.

The witness has given a detailed testimony with respect to the inquiry conducted by him to ascertain the genuineness of the passport which was held by the pax Maninder Singh (PO) and how he confirmed the fact that the passport belongs to some other person by vising the French Embassy, where he met the father of the original passport holder i.e. Sh.
Mohan Raj and thus, it was confirmed that accused apprehended was Maninder Singh who impersonated Mohan Raj Praveen to travel on his passport.

sentences.text:
The testimony of PW-2 gets corroborated through the testimony of PW-5 Inspector Afsar Raza,
who arrested the accused Maninder Singh and conducted the investigation by confirming the flight details of the accused Maninder as well as of the accused Kuldeep.
Therefore, it is clearly established by the prosecution that the accused Maninder had traveled on the passport of one Mohan Raj Praveen.

20. Since, the accused Maninder Singh is already PO, no further discussion as to his role is required and the role of the present accused is to be ascertained with respect to his ABHISHEK KUMAR FIR No. 437/2004 State v. Maninder Singh & Anr KUMAR Date:
2024.01.16 Page No:- 8 16:47:05 +0530 involvement in the criminal conspiracy.

The accused Kuldeep Singh did not dispute his arrest, disclosure statement, personal search memo, RPO report, EFRRO report with confirmation of arrival and departure,
verification report of UK visa and passport report of Kuldeep Singh.

Therefore, it is to be analyzed whether the accused Kuldeep Singh has conspired with the accused Maninder Singh (PO) for facilitating the journey of Maninder Singh to abroad on the basis of the passport of some other person.

21. In order to prove the conspiracy, the prosecution has firstly relied upon the departure details of the accused i.e. Ex.P-6 to show that the accused Kuldeep Singh was traveling on the same date and flight, in which the accused Maninder Singh was traveling and both of them were together deported from Dubai in the same flight.

Secondly, the prosecution were relying upon the witnesses namely Shakti Singh, who was the father of the accused Maninder Singh and had given statement U/s 161 Cr.P.C that accused Kuldeep had taken money from them for sending his son abroad and also on the statement of Sh. Vinod Bhatia, who had cut the hair and beard of the accused Maninder Singh at the instance of accused Kuldeep Singh.
However, the prosecution was unable to secure the appearance of both the witnesses before the Court and thus, they were dropped from the list of witnesses.

22. Apart from above witnesses, the prosecution has ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR Date:
FIR No. 437/2004 State v. Maninder Singh & Anr 2024.01.16 16:47:14 +0530 Page No:- 9 relied upon the testimony of Sh. Arvind Kumar Sharma, who was the employee of the hotel Virat Tourist Lodge to establish that accused Maninder Singh stayed at this hotel on 05.08.2004 and the arrangements were made by accused Kuldeep Singh.
The above-mentioned witness was examined as PW-4 but he did not support the case of the prosecution and was cross-examined by Ld. APP for the State.
The witness failed to identify the accused Kuldeep Singh and voluntarily stated that the accused never used to make payments for the persons staying in their hotel.
The witness denied that he has given any statement to the IO U/s 161 Cr.P.C.
During cross-examination by the counsel for the accused, the witness stated that there was no CCTV camera in their hotel and no record/register was seized from their hotel by the IO.
Thus, the statement of the witness does not support the case of the prosecution.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter the prosecution has also examined PW-1 Sh. Pawan Oberoi to establish the letter dated 29.10.2004 which is Ex.PW1/A and invoice no. 1477 dated 28.09.2004 which is Mark 1/A1.
The letter pertains to the fact that tickets were issued in favour of Kuldeep Singh and Parveen Raj Mohan and the tickets were booked by Kuldeep Singh.
During the cross-examination, the witness stated that the police did not record his statement and he did not meet any police official.
He further stated that he does not remember the name of the staff who prepared the Ex.PW1/A and invoice Mark 1/A1.

He also stated that he does not know the ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR Date:
2024.01.16 16:47:23 +0530 FIR No. 437/2004 State v. Maninder Singh & Anr Page No:- 10 accused Kuldeep Singh and he signed the letter Ex.PW1/A randomly.

24 . The testimony of the witness mentioned above was relevant from the point of view to establish the conspiracy as it would have been a connecting dot in the commission of the conspiracy and the subsequent acts but the testimony of the witness is not reliable and suffers from material infirmities.
Firstly, the witness could not bring on record any register or document of the agency to establish the issuance of the letter and secondly, no statement of the witness was recorded by the IO.
Thus, the testimony of the witness is not found to be sufficient to establish the case of the prosecution in the absence of other corroborating material.

25. After going through the entire record and the testimony of the witnesses, I am of the firm opinion that the prosecution has not been able to establish the case against the accused Kuldeep Singh beyond reasonable doubt.
Mere presence of the accused in the same flight and subsequent deportation is not enough to establish the chain of the conspiracy.
Further, the statement of the father of the pax Maninder Singh is only against the accused Kuldeep Singh and does not implicate the accused Maninder Singh.
Thus, the testimony is inherently not sufficient to establish the charge of the conspiracy but appears to be a case of cheating with the father of the accused which is not the case.
Also, Shakti Singh never stepped into the witness box to establish the allegations against the accused Kuldeep Singh.
ABHISHEK KUMAR  KUMAR

Date:
 2024.01.16 FIR No. 437/2004 State v. Maninder Singh & Anr 16:47:31 +0530 Page 26.

Furthermore, none of the prosecution witnesses could establish the chain of evidence which could as a whole established the charge of conspiracy as meeting of minds could not be proved in the instant case between the accused persons.
Also, the prosecution could not highlight the contravention of the provisions of the Passport Act by the accused Kuldeep Singh and thus, charge qua the same is not sustainable against him.
Due to the want of evidence, benefit of doubt is being given to the accused.
Accordingly, the accused Kuldeep Singh S/o Sh. Gurcharan Singh stands acquitted for offennce U/s 419 r/w Section 120-B IPC and 12 PP Act.
